findings.title: Submission-package items not present in the manuscript file

findings.title: Appendix B does not say which record set its 113 covers
findings.detail: Line 469 reads 'Appendix B uses the 113 recorded five-condition determinations'. Section 6.5 line 283 has just told the reader that fifteen records carried at least one label and that ten form the analysed set, so an unqualified 113 reads as the global total. Recommended: name the record set in the same clause.

findings.title: The credits use a denominator that cannot ever be completed
findings.detail: The Acknowledgments credit block at line 597 says 'Of the twenty-five reliability raters, three have confirmed'. Seventeen of those twenty-five are bench reviewers whose codes were generated in the browser and were never bound to an identity, so they cannot confirm, cannot be named, and are not pending. The denominator implies twenty-two outstanding confirmations that will never arrive. Recommended: 'Of the eight invited expert raters, three have confirmed and three elected to be named', with a clause recording that the other raters took part anonymously by design.

findings.title: Self-conscious phrasing flagged by the master prompt
findings.detail: 6 instance(s). The master prompt names these specifically and asks for direct methodological language where the underlying point is sound: 'stated plainly' line 216; 'read honestly' line 178; 'we accept it' line 166; 'The correct reading' line 294; 'not noise' line 259; 'as plainly as we know how' line 41

findings.title: Reference entries never cited in the body

findings.title: Section 6.5 pairs a ten-record count with a fifteen-record label count
findings.detail: Location A, Section 6.5 line 283, prints the regular-reviewer row as Records 10 and Labels 68, and says the ten analysed records 'carry 113 submitted determinations, reduced to 104'. Location B, research/current_reliability_2026-08-18.json, the file that produced the printed coefficients, reports the regular group as labels=68 with records_with_any_label=15, records_estimable=10 and records_single_rater=5. recompute_current_ac1.py::block sets 'labels' to len(rows) over every row in the group, so 68 spans all 15 records that group labelled, not the 10 that enter the coefficient. 104 is 36 + 68 and therefore spans fifteen records too. The ten-record deduplicated count is 104 less the 5 single-rater labels, that is 99. The 2026-08-04 analysed-set extract carries exactly 99 rows over ten records with no single-rater record, which corroborates 99 as the ten-record figure. Nature of the discrepancy: a record count and a label count from different record sets are printed on the same table row and in the same sentence. The expert row is unaffected because that group has no single-rater record. Evidence required: the 2026-08-18 per-record five-condition label counts, split into the ten estimable records and the five single-rater records. Recommended correction: keep 104 where it is described as the deduplicated five-condition set, state that it spans fifteen records, and give the ten-record analysed set its own number in the table. Do NOT change 104, 68 or 113 without those counts.

findings.title: Sixteen excluded labels are attributed to three excluded raters
findings.detail: Section 4.9 line 226 excludes 'Sixteen labels'; Section 6.5 line 281 attributes the exclusion to 'Three regular reviewers'. Sixteen labels from three raters is arithmetically possible and is probably correct, but the paper never states labels per rater, so a reviewer cannot check it. Evidence required: the per-rater baseline label counts. Recommended: state both numbers in one place, for example 'sixteen labels from three raters'.

findings.title: Journal requirements must be verified, never recalled
findings.detail: Master prompt Section 21 and absolute rule 13 forbid stating a journal's current requirements from memory. Before submission, open the target journal's own author guidance and check word limit, abstract structure, reference style, declaration wording and supplementary-file policy against this package. No requirement is asserted here because none has been verified in this run.

findings.title: Reference-classification independence
findings.detail: The automated raters were briefed by the authors on what 'grounded' and 'unsupported' mean. Section 4.4 says so. Confirm no sentence added since the last audit gives the reproduction more authority than that.

findings.title: Provenance memorandum
findings.detail: Section 4.3 states that record-level generation provenance was not retained. Decide whether the package carries a provenance-status memorandum marking each field Known, Partially recoverable, or Not recoverable. Do not reconstruct provenance retrospectively and present it as contemporaneous.

findings.title: Residual investigator dependence
findings.detail: After the stated mitigations, name what remains: corpus authorship, the operationalisation encoded in the key, and the absence of an independent validation adjudicator. Confirm Section 9 still names all three.

findings.title: Archive completeness
findings.detail: Confirm, with documentary evidence rather than recollection, that every reported number can be regenerated from retained materials. The known gap is the per-pass execution record for the three automated reference passes, which Section 4.4 states was not retained.

findings.title: Adjacent-construct distinctions are theorised
findings.detail: The Section 2.2 table asserts eight distinctions. None is empirically demonstrated by this study. Confirm the surrounding prose still presents them as conceptual argument rather than as findings.

findings.title: Falsification answer
findings.detail: The author must be able to state what result would falsify or materially weaken the interpretation. Confirm an answer exists in the defence briefing before any interview or review response.
